newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN CINEMA -- Latest weekly box office.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN CINEMA -- Latest weekly box office.

text.p: INDIAN FILM BOX OFFICE REPORT FOR WEEK TO SEPT 26, 1996
Four films and disastrous results was the box-office fate of the week. DAANVEER (Generous Donor), a Mithun Chakraborty-Rambha starrer, was below average because of lack of novelty in the story.

DUSHMAN DUNIYA KA (Enemy of the World) directed by ace comedian of yesteryear, Mehmood, could neither entertain nor give any cinematic satisfaction though it tried to provide an insight into drug abuse. As director Mehmood had produced some hilarious films like Kunwara Baap and Bhoot Bungalow decades ago, expectations were high on humour. Thus the result was below 50 percent average collections, though limited number of prints were released.
ZULM HI ZULM (Tyranny), a mediocre film, had a poor collection. BHOOT (Dubbed version of Evil Dead 2) failed to shake the audience and thus was rejected.

HINDUSTANI and JEET maintained their top position on the chart as No.2 and No. 3 even this week. Heavy drops were seen in ANGAARA (from 10 million rupees last week to two million rupees), SAZAA-E-KAALA PAANI (3.2 million rupees to 1.7 million rupees) and BAL BRAMHCHARI (2.7 million rupees to 0.8 million rupees).
MISSION IMPOSSIBLE (English and Hindi versions) was released on September 27 with good response. Even THE NET looks like a strong contender on the strength of star attraction Sandra Bullock.
EXECUTIVE DECISION continued to draw good houses everywhere. BROKEN ARROW remained an average grosser in Mumbai.
